title: Compact fidelity bundles — commercial playbook and migration kit
author: Maya Chen
summary: A practical commercial playbook and migration kit for launching Compact Fidelity Bundles (CFB): smaller, predictable fidelity packages designed to reduce onboarding friction for developers and SMB customers while protecting unit economics and enabling staged upsells.
content:
Overview

This document describes the Compact Fidelity Bundles (CFB) product concept, pricing rules, packaging options, migration and rollout playbook, telemetry and acceptance criteria, and sample customer comms. CFBs are a new set of small-step fidelity packages intended to: 
- Lower friction for low-volume customers and dev teams to adopt higher-fidelity features.
- Provide a predictable, meterable commercial construct that integrates with existing crediting and SLA systems.
- Allow controlled upsell paths to larger fidelity SKUs and Dedicated capacity.

Goals & guiding principles

1) Reduce activation friction: make it easy for developers to buy useful fidelity increments without enterprise procurement.
2) Preserve economic invariants: bundle pricing should not materially worsen Redwood unit economics — targeted discounts are capped and conditional.
3) Operational simplicity: map bundles directly to existing billing and quota enforcement primitives to avoid custom plumbing.
4) Experiment-first rollout: A/B test pricing and expiry policies; instrument success metrics and rollback thresholds.

Scope and out-of-scope

- Included: CFB product definitions, pricing bands, eligibility rules, migration steps for existing microbundle customers, telemetry keys, playbook for sales and CS, and sample email templates.
- Excluded: Dedicated/Private bespoke commercial agreements (those remain negotiated separately).

Bundle definitions (table)

| Bundle SKU | Duration | Token budget | Typical use case | Price (USD) | Auto-renew | Notes |
|------------|----------|--------------|------------------|------------:|----------:|------|
| CFB-XS | 30 days | 250K tokens | Developer experimentation, prototypes | $9 | Optional | Non-refundable, trial cap 1 per account |
| CFB-S | 30 days | 1M tokens | Early-stage product integration, light traffic | $29 | Optional | Eligible for 10% first-time bundle discount |
| CFB-M | 90 days | 5M tokens | Production pilot, moderate throughput | $119 | Optional | Includes basic telemetry credits (14 days retention) |
| CFB-L | 365 days | 25M tokens | SMB production, predictable monthly use | $899 | Manual renewal | Volume discount bucket available on commit |

Pricing rules and guardrails

- Anchor price per 1M tokens is used to compute effective discounts. Discount caps: 20% for first-quarter introductory offers, 10% for standard volume credits applied retroactively.
- Bundles do not change model-tier pricing (eg. different model variants still consume token budgets differently).
- Apply a per-account additive safety margin check: if measured average tokens-per-session > bundle's expected sessions x session budget, flag candidate for upgrade nudges.
- Bundles are mapped to existing billing SKUs with prefix CFB- so they leverage existing invoice and entitlement machinery.

Eligibility and constraints

- Publicly available to self-serve signups and credit-card customers.
- Enterprise accounts with active negotiated contracts must purchase via their account rep to preserve contract terms.
- Limit: one concurrent CFB-XS per account. All other bundles can be stacked subject to a 3-bundle soft limit; stacking triggers an automated review if combined annualized spend > $15k.

Technical & billing integration checklist

1) Billing: create new SKU mappings in the billing catalog (billing.skus.CFB_*). Owner: Finance/Billing (owner: Priya Nair). Due: 2026-12-10.
2) Quota enforcement: map bundle token budgets to per-account quota entries in QuotaService v2 (quota_key: cfb.tokens.<account_id>). Owner: Runtime (owner: Linh Tran).
3) Entitlements: proxy existing credit ledger events to include bundle origin (event.metadata.bundle_sku). Owner: Platform Product.
4) Console UX: add bundle purchase modal, bundle usage timeline, upgrade CTA. Owner: Developer Experience.

Migration playbook (existing microbundle or ad-hoc credit customers)

Objective: reduce friction for customers currently on legacy microbundles or ad-hoc top-ups to migrate to CFB while avoiding revenue cliffs.

Step-by-step migration (for Sales / CS)

1) Detection: run query to identify accounts where current microbundle monthly spend <= $1,000 and last 90-day usage pattern matches target CFB profile. Telemetry: billing.account_monthly_spend, usage.eligible_for_cfb=true.
2) Soft-offer email + Console banner (7-day trial coupon CFB-S at 50% off) — template in Appendix. Responsible: Growth Marketing.
3) Trial conversion flow: if customer redeems, record event billing.bundle_redeemed with referral=csm.offer. If conversion <10% after 30 days, escalate to Sales adoption play.
4) Auto-migration (opt-in): for customers who explicitly choose auto-migrate, compute remaining credit equivalence using conversion rules below and create entitlement.

Credit conversion rules (examples)

- Legacy microbundle credits are converted to token budgets by: tokens = legacy_credits * conversion_rate. Conversion rates are set quarterly by Finance (current: 1 credit = 1,200 tokens).
- Near-term protection: if conversion would cause a >30% immediate loss of billed value to Redwood, apply a 30-day staged top-up to make up for delta.

Rollout phases and acceptance criteria

Phase 0 — Lab (2 weeks): internal QA and synthetic traffic test. Success: error rate <0.5% on quota mapping and correct billing events emitted.
Phase 1 — Canary (4 weeks): 1% of new signups and 2 pilot customers. Success metrics: 20% trial redemption rate, <3% billing disputes.
Phase 2 — Regional ramp (6–8 weeks): open to US/EU markets. Acceptance: NRR impact neutral, conversion >= 12% for trial cohorts.
Phase 3 — Global GA: open to all. Monitor monthly.

Telemetry, dashboards and SLOs

- Required telemetry events: billing.bundle_purchased, billing.bundle_redeemed, usage.cfb_token_consumed (per-token emission aggregated by minute), billing.dispute_opened, account.migration_opt_in.
- Console dashboards to build: CFB adoption funnel (impressions -> purchase -> redemption -> upgrade), per-bundle revenue run-rate, dispute rate by SKU.
- SLOs (operational): billing_event_delivery >= 99.9% within 2 minutes; quota_enforcement_latency p95 < 150ms; conversion pipeline ETL delay < 10 minutes.

Commercial experimentation matrix

- Variables to A/B test: first-offer discount (20%/10%/none), trial duration (7/14 days), auto-renew default (on/off), stack limit (2 vs 3 bundles).
- Primary metrics: trial->paid conversion, net revenue retention (90 days), average ticket size, support ticket rate per 1k customers.

Sales & CS playbook snippets

- Discovery questions: "What's your predictable monthly token need?", "Are you trying to reduce latency or improve response fidelity?".
- Upgrade triggers: 3 consecutive months hitting >80% of CFB token budget; automated upgrade recommendation in Console and a Sales-ready quote with CFB-M or Dedicated options.
- Refund policy: non-refundable; exceptions escalated to Finance for credits > $1k annualized.

Customer communications (examples)

- Console banner: short CTA: "Try a Compact Fidelity Bundle — 1M tokens for $29, 30-day trial available" with link to FAQ.
- Email (trial offer): Subject: "Reduce friction — try Compact Fidelity Bundles at 50% off". Body: 3 bullets explaining benefits, link to one-click purchase, contact your CSM. Template in Appendix.

Legal & compliance checklist

- Ensure billing SKU text appears in invoices and matches contractual language for regulated customers. Legal sign-off required for any promotional extensions >30 days. Owner: Legal (owner: Daniel Kwan).
- Data residency: CFB entitlements must include region tag; ensure Private deployments are excluded from self-serve purchase flows unless explicitly enabled.

Rollback conditions and mitigation steps

- Immediate disable if billing disputes exceed 5% of transactions in a rolling 7-day window. Mitigation: pause new purchases, present upgrade-only path for existing customers, run reconciliation.
- If quota enforcement regression occurs (p95 latency > 250ms), roll back quota mapping changes and revert to previous enforcement endpoint.

Appendix

A. Sample console copy (short)
"Compact Fidelity Bundles give small teams predictable fidelity without a long contract. Pick a bundle, start in minutes."

B. Sample email template (trial offer)

Hello {first_name},
We built Compact Fidelity Bundles so teams like yours can experiment with better responses without a heavy commitment. For a limited time redeem CFB-S at 50% off. Click here to start.

C. Event names & schema (examples)
- billing.bundle_purchased: {account_id, bundle_sku, price_usd, timestamp}
- usage.cfb_token_consumed: {account_id, bundle_sku, tokens, model_variant, request_id, timestamp}
- billing.dispute_opened: {account_id, invoice_id, reason}
(Implementers: include these keys in telemetry schema registry)
